one_liner: Netlify has a broad REST API with OAuth2 and self-serve personal access tokens. The pages given don't confirm the free-plan terms or the vendor MCP server, so those fields are low confidence.
auth_notes: Personal access tokens are generated in user settings and sent as a Bearer token. Public integrations must use OAuth2, with an app registered in user settings.
access_notes: Self-serve PAT generation and OAuth app registration are confirmed by the docs. The fetched pages say nothing about pricing or free-plan limits. The self_serve_free label is inferred from the self-serve credential flow and is low confidence. The partner pages concern revenue-share and startup programs, not API access.
blocker_notes: No blocker is shown in the pages. Free-plan credit limits could not be verified from them.

evidence.quote: If you’re making a public integration with Netlify for others to enjoy, you must use OAuth2.
Use your PAT for manual authentication in shell scripts or commands that use the Netlify API.
You can register a new application in your Netlify user settings for [OAuth applications](https://app.netlify.com/applications).
Use the Netlify REST API to manage atomic deploys of your sites and apps, manage form submissions, inject JavaScript snippets, manage DNS, and so much more.
You can browse the [OpenAPI reference for the Netlify API](https://open-api.netlify.com) to explore available endpoints.
